content:
ashley: Heads-up — after rolling mixed-quant kernels (fp8 + int8-fallback) to canary, our structured-output evals spiked with hallucinations and broken JSON in downstream tasks. rolling back for now but want a quick triage. :warning:
triage-bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T07:20: applied mixed-quant kernel set: kernel:v2.4-quant, routing:mix-heuristic-3, calib-table:calib-v1. (Canary -> 10% hosts)
yang: Thanks. What metrics are you seeing? numbers?
ashley: Eval suite: onboarding_json_tests (1k examples) — exact-key extraction F1 down 4.1 pts, valid-JSON fraction down from 0.986 -> 0.868 (12% invalid), hallucination rate +6.3% (per eval rubric). Latency improved ~22% p50 tokens but some tail latency jitter.
maria: Do we have a repro script + config? can we repro locally with same batch shapes?
ashley: Yes — repro command I used: 
```
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/repro_eval.py \
  --model redwood/gptx-13b \
  --kernel-profile kernel:v2.4-quant \
  --quant-config configs/quant/mix-fp8-int8.json \
  --calib calib/calib-v1.json \
  --batch-shapes "[(1,32),(4,256),(8,128)]" \
  --eval-set tests/onboarding_json
```

ashley: Attached a short log, suspicious lines: 
```
[2026-03-16 07:21:12] kv_cache: miss-ratio 0.18 (expected 0.02)
[2026-03-16 07:21:12] batching: split-policy changed from auto->heuristic-3 due to min-latency config
[2026-03-16 07:21:13] kernel-select: chosen fp8-kernel (matmul_opt_v3) fallback int8 for softmax at seq>512
```

devon: kv miss ratio that high is interesting — could be cache key hashing differences when using quantized kernels (different tokenization offsets?) or a bug in KV pack/align when using fp8 path. any diffs in KV index generation?
yang: I profiled with nsys — sending top block timings and memory ops: 
```
# aggregate sample (canary host):
matmul_fp8 kernel: 42% time
softmax_int8: 18% time
kv_pack: 6% time (extra memcpy)
copy_align: 7% time (memset?)
```

yang: Also saw extra memcpy around kv_pack when sequence shorter than 64 — looks like an alignment pad for fp8 lanes. maybe pad code path invalidating dense KV keys.
maria: Could calibration (calib-v1) be shifting quantization bins such that logits for structured delimiters (like "---JSON---") change shape and tokenization hits unk tokens -> unpredictable generation?
ashley: We inspected token-level diffs: delim tokens kept, but attention scores around delim tokens have higher variance in fp8 run vs float32 — softmax stability might be degraded. Also saw more frequent fallback to int8 softmax at seq>512 which wasn't expected.

kim: Suggest steps: 1) pin kernel to fp32 matmul + fp8-only softmax locally to see if matmul_fp8 is culprit; 2) run eval with KV cache disabled to confirm cache involvement; 3) run with calibration skew (apply +/- 5% scale) to see sensitivity; 4) collect couple of failing examples and token-level attention logits for float32 vs quant run. I can take 1+2.

yang: I'll run nsys traces with nvtx on the kernel boundaries and dump KV packing buffers (hex) for comparison. I'll also diff the calibrated scale tensors between calib-v1 and float-run.
devon: I'll put a quick canary that disables automatic split-policy -> force batch shapes frequency to previous default, to rule out batching heuristic regression.
maria: For reproducer we should include the exact host env: cuda 12.2, cudnn 9.1, driver 545.68, and compiled kernel flags: -O3 -mfma. I saw one host in canary with cuda 12.1 which had different fallback behavior.
ashley: I'll collect 20 failing examples (saved under gs://redwood-triage/quant/1823456789/). Also adding eval diffs and sample outputs.

triage-bot: Action items assigned: kim -> local repro (kv off + fp32 matmul), yang -> nsys + kv dump, devon -> batching policy rollback test, ashley -> failing examples + logs. ETA 24h. (reacted with :clipboard:)

yang: quick note — if it's kv alignment, we might see corruption only for long contexts with mix of batch shapes (the kv buffer packing assumes 32-bit alignment for fp32; fp8 path packs differently). watch out for packing offsets in packing.cu: function pack_kv_block().

maria: Agreed. Also flagging this to eng-ml to see if eval suite needs more structured delim tests. @eng-ml please weigh in.

ashley: Thanks all. rolling rollback fully now and will post updates in this thread once we have repros. :thumbsup:
